title: withdrawFrom() Balance Check Caps Surplus Extraction at Principal Amount
rootCause: AYieldStrategy.withdrawFrom() at line 292 checks this.balanceOf(token, client) >= amount, where balanceOf() returns principalOf() (principal only). The child _withdrawFrom() correctly checks amount <= surplus. But when surplus exceeds principal (>100% yield), the parent check reverts before the child check is reached, permanently locking the excess surplus.
impact: Surplus beyond 100% of principal becomes permanently unextractable through withdrawFrom()/SurplusWithdrawer. For a client with 1000 principal and 1500 surplus, only 1000 of surplus can be extracted. The remaining 500 is locked until totalWithdrawal. This also means balanceOf() is marked DEPRECATED in the interface but is used for a critical access-control decision.
recommendation: Change line 292 to use this.totalBalanceOf(token, client) instead of this.balanceOf(token, client). Or remove the redundant parent check entirely since _withdrawFrom enforces its own surplus constraint.
